criteria.evidence: Three OS jobs (linux/ubuntu-latest, macos/macos-latest, windows/windows-latest) written as explicit jobs rather than strategy.matrix; functionally one job per OS as the user requested in turn 1 and approved.

windows job runs `pwsh -File scripts/install.ps1 -Channel nightly` with a newly created scripts/install.ps1; invoked from checkout rather than irm|iex, disclosed with a comment and in the turn-1 summary.
All three jobs use actions/checkout with `ref: main`.

Loop runs `mise run test:e2e --agent "$agent" TestPartialStaging` for claude-code opencode factoryai-droid cursor-cli copilot-cli roger-roger codex; gemini-cli excluded with hooksPath reason; Windows limited to claude-code with stated reason.
TestPartialStaging chosen: 'prompt 1 → commit → wait for checkpoint 1 → prompt 2 → commit → checkpoint 2'.
Turn 0 reply surveys e2e tests and explains why TestPartialStaging is the only exact 2-prompt match.
Turn 0 reply lists e2e.yml, e2e-windows.yml, e2e-isolated.yml, nightly.yml, e2e-checkpoints-v2.yml before proposing a plan.
Per-agent runs happen in a sequential `for agent in $AGENTS` loop inside each OS job; no agent matrix.
'Committed locally as b960207f on add-nightly-matrix-e2e-test ... no origin remote ... can't push the branch or open the draft PR'.

judge.reason: The replay delivers a nightly-scheduled workflow covering all three OSes with the correct per-OS install paths, a single two-prompt checkpoint test run per agent inside each OS job, checkout of main, and a local commit with the PR limitation explained. Doubt remains because the OS coverage is three hand-written jobs rather than a literal strategy.matrix, the Windows installer is invoked from the checkout rather than as if published, and pi/vogon are not explicitly excluded with a reason.
